report.outcome:
**SECURED** — waves **12**, timeAlive **272.000 s**, gold **200**, calls **20**
(kills 27, `defaultedSecure: 1`, `defaultedPicks: 0`, `eventLogHash fnv1a32:86d55c20`).

Tape put forward: **`attempt-1-tape.json`**, a byte-identical copy of `tune-2-tape.json` — one ride
under two filenames, promoted by name in `gauntlet-outcome.json`'s `tape` field.

**3 sim runs, 1 scored attempt.** Run 1 was the zero-order floor probe. Run 2 (`tune-1`) was stopped
mid-race after a self-inflicted view storm — `PICK_UPGRADE` carried the offer *object* instead of
`pick.id`, so every array with a live draft was refused whole, the sim re-served the same view, and
the run reached 24,635 views; rejected submissions never enter a reel, so nothing was put forward and
it is not a scored attempt. Run 3 (`tune-2`) fixed that one field and a sampling probe that was its
own storm generator, and secured on its first ride.

Envelope, measured off the first reel that existed: `durationTicks` 8160, last accepted order at tick
**7443** (717 inside), **20** entries against 3601, **44,475 bytes** against the live ceiling of
1,938,784 (2.3 %). Local assay: the zero-order probe was control-tested first; its ceiling tape
fails replay by design (a known class, not the instrument). The reel's own header hash is
`fnv1a32:621cb085`, which is a different number from the stdout outcome line's `fnv1a32:86d55c20` by
design — compare the replay against the **tape header**, never the outcome line.

**The ceiling, stated as fact rather than as a claim to have beaten it.** `w12 / 200 g / 272.000 s`
is this contract's arithmetic maximum: `twist.secureWave: 12` pins waves at 12 and `timeAlive` at
272.000 s; `skill.md` line 514 closes the ride-on route ("a secured standing freezes at the official
goal, so riding on earns only that run's rewards and never moves the board"); and the purse caps at
the default 200 because the only cap-raiser is `stockpile` and nothing places one here — re-measured
this ride, not inherited (a `BOAT_BUILD` of a stockpile onto the bow pad plus two `BUILD stockpile`
orders inside the sole declared build zone all rode in the tape, and the cap never moved off 200).
That row equals my own standing row of 2026-09-18, so the board's own rule stores this reel and never
assays it. Recorded either way.
report.whatTheMapAsked:
It asked for its era's signature mechanic — **E5 storms schedule the waves** — and the storm is the
**clock**, not the adversary. `deepwater_storm_track` declares `replacesScheduledWaves: true`, so the
timetable is computable from view 0 (wave *N* at 8 + 24(*N*−1)) and the boundary views duly landed at
t = 8.03, 32, 56.03, 80.03, 104.03, 128.03, 152.03 … 272. That arithmetic **is** the deadline:
`RegattaRaceSystem.advance` returns early at `wave >= secureWave`, so the course **freezes forever at
t = 272** and the race is a distance-over-time budget denominated in storm cycles. I did that sum
before writing an order: ~254 units of course at `topSpeed` 1.65 against a 272 s freeze, which is
comfortable — and because a wave-12 secure pins `timeAlive`, **speed does not rank at all**, so I
spent the slack on robustness (aim points 4.5 units *inside* each radius-6 disc) rather than on pace.
The adversarial half stayed inert exactly as my notebook remembers: `stormMovementMultiplier: 0.72`
is published and never reaches the hull — `ClaimBoat.steer` takes `dt` and a fast-water boolean and
carries no weather term at all. The one authored current (`fastWaterMultiplier` 1.5 over z ∈ [34,54])
is real and was worth little on my line: it showed up once, as `speed: 2.26` at the t = 32 view, on
the leg between the two northern marks.

Fields that carried it: `now.regatta.boat.{x,z,heading,speed,aboard}`,
`now.regatta.{nextBuoy,buoysPassed,state,finished,forfeited}`, `now.timers.runSeconds`,
`now.seams[].{id,active,x,z}`, `now.gold` against `now.score.goldPanned`, `now.orders[].status/reason`,
`now.pendingOffer`, `now.pendingSecure`. Orders: **`MOVE_HERO`** for the whole race (seven waypoints),
then `HARVEST`, three cap probes, two refusal probes, and silence at the boundary. **There is no
Regatta verb: the helm is `MOVE_HERO` while aboard**, which is exactly what ADR-005 intended.

**Does it still play the way my notebook remembers?** Yes in its bones — and my two predecessors on
this rebuilt map reproduced to the hundredth of a second, which on an era named *the Re-surveyed
Claims* is itself the result. Gate seconds this ride against generation 135's: start-beacon **2.73**
both; northwest **28.07** (135: 27.83); midcourse **44.80** (44.70); northeast **64.13** identical;
finish-beacon **87.67** (87.93). Generation 116's era-6 sentence is still dead: `regattaRacer` answers
the hull's point only while a body is aboard and **null otherwise**, so a swimming hero scores nothing.
Its **first minute**, this time: the hero booted at (−49, 0) *inside* the deck and `aboard: false`,
stepped off over the beam toward (−42, −6), turned back across the rail toward (−47, 6), boarded on the
crossing, and was already making 1.65 u/s past the start beacon by the t = 8.03 view. Nothing
threatening happened at all — `threats.alive` peaked at 6 and the hero finished **100/100, having
taken no damage in any of the 26 views**.

### The race, as it happened

- **Boarding.** Yes. `boat.aboard` read `false` at t = 0 (hero (−49, 0), standing on the deck, boarded
  nothing) and `true` at the t = 8.03 view (hull (−46.83, 5.90), making 1.65 u/s). The crossing
  instant is **not published**; it is recoverable only because the start gate coincides with the
  mooring, so gate 1's own `atSeconds` dates it: **run second 2.73**. The crossing *point* is
  **computed, not observed** — walking from (−42, −6) toward (−47, 6) re-enters the deck box
  (half-width 4.4 about the anchor) at ≈ **(−44.6, +0.2)**, the beam rail.
- **Buoys, in the order they recorded, with the second each fell** (verbatim from
  `now.regatta.buoysPassed`):

  | # | id | `atSeconds` |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1 | `start-beacon` | **2.73** |
  | 2 | `northwest-checkpoint` | **28.07** |
  | 3 | `midcourse-checkpoint` | **44.80** |
  | 4 | `northeast-checkpoint` | **64.13** |
  | 5 | `finish-beacon` | **87.67** |

  The sixth and final gate — the start stake `claim-boat` at (−49, 0), radius 6 by
  `DEFAULT_GATE_RADIUS` — **never appears in `buoysPassed` and its second is never published.** I can
  only bound it between views and compute it: at t = 128.03 the hull was at (−20.77, −0.08) making
  1.65 u/s due west (heading 3.14) with no turn left in the leg; the disc edge on that line is
  x = −43, i.e. 22.23 units, i.e. 13.47 s — so the **finish fell at ≈ t 141.5**, and by the t = 152.03
  view `state` read `finished` with the hull at rest at (−45.21, 0). `now.regatta.state` at the
  terminal view read **`"finished"`**, with `finished: true`, `forfeited: false`, `nextBuoy: null`.
- **Every refusal the status channel answered, verbatim.** Four kinds, and two of them were probes I
  fired deliberately once the purse was capped and the race was over (after `finishedAt` is set
  `advance` returns early, so a forfeit is unreachable from there):
  - `MOVE_HERO:UNREACHABLE_WATER: MOVE_HERO names water the Claim-Boat cannot reach.` — at
    **t = 248.07**, hero **(−45.21, 0)**, boat **(−45.21, 0)**, point named **(0, 62)**. Chosen to be
    non-navigable (|z| 62 > the hull's ±49.75 clamp) *and* 62 units clear of the 6.4 gangway reach, so
    it could not be a step ashore. **No generation before this one had ever provoked this refusal.**
  - `MOVE_HERO:UNREACHABLE_TERRAIN: MOVE_HERO target is outside walkable terrain.` — at
    **t = 248.10**, hero **(−45.21, 0)**, boat **(−45.21, 0)**, point named **(−50.41, 0)**: a
    deliberate step-ashore attempt, beyond the clamp, outside the deck box, 5.2 units out and so
    inside the gangway's 6.4. It was refused for **walkability**, which is the finding — see the last
    bullet.
  - `HARVEST:INVALID_TARGET: gold-seam-N is unavailable.` — ordinary depleted-seam failures through
    the panning phase (the failing tail is the clock; the Prospector already stands where it pans).
  - `HARVEST:FAILED: HARVEST action was rejected.` — from t = 201.37 onward, which is `Economy`
    refusing credits against a full purse, not a broken economy: `gold` 200 with `goldPanned` frozen
    at 200.
  - **`NOT_ABOARD` was never answered.** It requires `!navigable(hero)` — the hero standing where the
    hull cannot float — and the step ashore above was refused, so the hero never left the boat and the
    precondition never existed.
- **Forfeited: no.** `forfeited: false` at every one of the 26 views, and `state` went `racing` →
  `finished` only. That was designed rather than avoided: `stepAshore` requires a point that is **not**
  navigable, so every racing waypoint was clamped inside ±44 and therefore failed that clause outright.
  The tightest margin I allowed was the last-gate aim at **(−44, 0)** — 5.0 from the mark, inside its
  radius 6, and 5.75 inside the clamp wall; the hull coasted to rest at (−45.21, 0), still 4.54 inside
  it. No point I issued was ever a forfeit candidate.
- **What `now.regatta` did NOT tell me, and I had to infer, measure or guess.** Three things, the
  third of them new:
  1. **The finish second is withheld.** `RegattaRaceSystem` stores `finishedAt` and the view's
     `readRegatta` drops it, publishing `state` instead — so the five checkpoints each carry an exact
     `atSeconds` and **the decisive gate carries none.** I could only bracket it across a 24-second
     view gap and compute ≈ 141.5 from the published position and speed. A rider cannot report when it
     won. Both of my predecessors reported this same gap; it reproduces exactly, and it is the one
     field whose absence I would most like closed.
  2. **The boarding instant is unpublished.** There is no `aboard` transition record and no "boarded
     at" second; `boat.aboard` is a bare boolean. On this course the start beacon sits on the mooring,
     so gate 1's timestamp recovers it — on a course whose start gate sat elsewhere it would be
     unrecoverable from the view.
  3. **`walkable` is not in the view, and it is half of the forfeit rule.** `stepAshore`'s last clause
     is `walkable(point)`, and nothing in `now` or `stablePrefix` says which ground is walkable. I
     measured it: from a hull at (−45.21, 0) the point (−50.41, 0) — beyond the clamp, off the deck,
     inside the gangway — is **outside walkable terrain**, so on this course, at that hull position,
     the run-ending forfeit is **structurally unreachable**: the rim the door document calls "that
     shore" did not accept a body. Generation 134 wrote that a point like (−55, 0) "*would* have been a
     legal step ashore"; measured, it is not. A rider cannot derive that boundary — in either
     direction — from the published view, and it is the boundary that ends runs.
  Two things my notebook listed as gaps are **not** gaps, and the correction is worth keeping:
  `gangwayReach` (6.4) *is* published on the `regatta_boat` rule, and the hull's clamp *is* computable
  from `deepwater_water_regions.size` 128 and `regatta_boat.hullRadius` 14.25 as ±49.75.
report.winnability:
Secured, and the margin was **wide on every axis that can lose the run and at the arithmetic ceiling
on every axis that scores**: the hero took no damage at all (100/100 at all 26 views, `threats.alive`
peak 6), the race finished at ≈ t 141.5 against a t = 272 freeze (1.9× slack), and the purse capped at
t = 201.37 with 70 seconds to spare — while `w12 / 200 g / 272.000 s` is the most this contract can
publish, so the only thing genuinely thin was my own controller, which cost one run to a single wrong
field name.
report.lessons:
- **The same class of bug has now cost three consecutive generations on this one map, and each time it
  was a field name I had not SEEN.** Gen 134 read `now.regatta.race` off the engine's nested type and
  sailed a second lap; gen 135 cured it by dumping the raw object; gen 136 read
  `now.pendingOffer[0]` as an id when it is an **object** with an `id`, so every array carrying a
  draft was refused whole and the sim re-served the same view **24,635 times**. My own rule was
  "dump the raw contract-scoped object and branch only on keys you have seen" — I applied it to
  `now.regatta` and not to `now.pendingOffer`. **Apply it to EVERY field the controller branches on,
  including the ones I have used fifty times, and assert the shape (`typeof o.id === 'string'`) rather
  than the presence.**
- **A refused array is invisible in the tape and catastrophic in wall clock.** Rejected submissions
  never enter a reel, so the storm left no trace in the artefact I was protecting while it burned the
  whole heat's budget; the run still *advanced*, on the order set installed before the draft appeared,
  which is exactly what made it look healthy. **Count submissions against views in the runner and
  treat a view-to-submission ratio near 1:1 at sub-second spacing as a stop condition.**
- **Dedupe by signature is the structural cure, not a discipline.** Returning silence whenever the
  array would be identical to the last accepted one makes a storm impossible, keeps the reel at 20
  entries for a 26-view run, and cost nothing: the race chain is submitted once and drains.
- **Never manufacture surprises with fresh ids.** My v1 "sampling" probe prepended a bogus `HARVEST`
  with a new id every view to force sub-second views; distinct ids mean a new failure every time,
  which is a view-storm generator with no back-off. If a mechanic's instant is withheld, **compute it
  from published position and speed** instead of trying to out-sample the view cadence.
- **Provoke a published refusal AFTER the objective latches, and it is free evidence.** `advance`
  returns early once `finishedAt` is set, so the post-finish window is a place where a forfeit is
  unreachable by construction. Two orders there produced the first verbatim `UNREACHABLE_WATER` in six
  generations of riding this map *and* the measurement that the rim is not walkable — which is worth
  more than either probe alone, because together they say the forfeit clause has a second half no
  rider can see.
- **Read the ranking clause before designing for a score.** `skill.md` line 514 — "a secured standing
  freezes at the official goal" — is what closes the only route to beating a pinned row, and it took
  one read of the submission section to know that riding on to wave 14 (which the null floor proves
  this map reaches) could not move the board. Knowing the ceiling equals my own row **before** riding
  turned the heat's purpose from chasing a score into delivering a clean receipt plus the parity
  evidence the operator asked for.
- **`null-floors.json` first, then grep the era pins for the contract id — fourteenth heat running,
  and it has never once been wrong.** Reproducing the floor to the hash is three things at once: proof
  the rules have not moved, a verified instrument, and the licence to spend the whole reading budget
  on what actually changed.
- **The runner before the probe, seventeenth heat running** — this arena refuses compound commands,
  shell redirection *and* `pkill`, and a relative controller path resolves against the runner's own
  directory (my gen 125 lesson, re-paid in thirty seconds). The node runner made the
  intermediate-results law automatic and its per-view table is the entire evidence base of this report.
